and sometimes `upstream prematurely closed connection`. Happened right after maintenance window at 02:10 UTC.
Alex (SRE): thanks, @Tina. Can you paste a full curl with `-v` and the x-request-id header from the customer? also want the edge logs for that rid.

infra-bot: notifier: cert-rotation job completed at 2026-03-17T02:09:43Z, rollout: canary->global
Jordan (Infra): interesting — client reports IPv6 addr in connect. asking DNS team for recent SRV/AAAA TTLs. @Alex can you share edge trace for rid_8f3b2?
Alex (SRE): edge trace shows upstream selection to pool `cust-us-east-1` and then `connect: i/o timeout` from proxy to selected upstream. No app error. Only after cert rotation window.
Tina (Support): I ran `dig` from our debug host: 
```
;; ANSWER SECTION:
api.redwood-inference.com. 30 IN CNAME api-eu.redwood-inference.net.
api-eu.redwood-inference.net. 20 IN SRV 0 5 443 pool3.eu.redwood.internal.
pool3.eu.redwood.internal. 20 IN AAAA 2607:f8b0:4006:80b::200e
pool3.eu.redwood.internal. 20 IN A 34.120.34.56
```
Tina (Support): note SRV TTL=20s, CNAME TTL=30s. low TTL.
Maria (Customer): we don't have IPv6 in our infra; curious why client picks IPv6.
Jordan (Infra): when resolver returns both AAAA and A, client stacks will prefer IPv6 if available. If AAAA points at a host not accepting TLS for this tenant (post-rotation config mismatch), handshake times out -> 502 returned by edge proxy. This smells like a split-brain between backend fleet states during rollout.
Alex (SRE): reproducing locally: forced AAAA-only connect to host above => `openssl s_client -connect [2607:f8b0:...]:443 -servername api.redwood-inference.com` hangs then `no peer certificate` after timeout. IPv4 connect works and returns cert chain for rotated cert.
Jordan (Infra): immediate mitigations:
- flush resolver cache on edge proxies to avoid stale SRV->AAAA mapping (we're seeing mixed state across proxies). command: `systemctl restart redwood-resolver` on edge (or `resolvectl flush-caches`).
- add temporary preference to prefer A records for this customer route (routing override)
- pause cert rotation for affected zone until backends reconcile
Alex (SRE): long term: increase SRV/CNAME TTL during rotation windows to allow safer switchover and ensure dual-stack config parity during cert rollouts. Also add health check gating per-IP before marking backend healthy.
Tina (Support): told customer we rolled a resolver flush and applied route override. asked them to test.
Maria (Customer): confirmed: after ~90s the 502s stopped. thank you, /cc @support-team :thumbsup:
Jordan (Infra): opened ticket with DNS provider for SRV caching anomalies. Also adding a playbook note for "cert rollout + dual-stack verification".
Alex (SRE): saving traces and reassigning to oncall for postmortem. Follow-up: check edge metrics for handshake timeouts vs cert-rotation windows.
Tina (Support): closing the customer escalation for now, will reopen if it reoccurs.
